name: The Twelve Gates
summary: The twelve gates of the New Jerusalem, each a single pearl, inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.

descriptors.statement: The twelve gates of the city are twelve pearls, each gate being made of a single pearl.
descriptors.symbolic_referent: The preciousness, purity, and singular costliness of access to God's eternal city — pearls in the ancient world were among the most valued materials and, unlike gold, are organic and singular rather than fabricated.

descriptors.statement: The names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel are inscribed on the twelve gates.

relations.notes: Twelve gates are part of the city walls (Rev 21:12).
